div.head: Hl 6
div.ab: Gif ceorl acwyle be libbendum wife ⁊ bearne, riht is þæt hit, þæt bearn, medder folgige, ⁊ him mon an his fæderingmagum wilsumne berigean gefelle, his feoh to healdenne, oþ þæt he X wintra sie.
Gif ceorl acwyle be libbendum wife ⁊ bearne, riht is þæt hit, þæt bearn, medder folgige; ⁊ him mon an his fæderingmagum wilsumne berigean geselle, his feoh to healdenne, oþ þæt he X wintra sie.
Gif ceorle acwyle be libbendum wife ⁊ bearne, riht is þæt hit, þæt bearn, medder folgige, ⁊ him man an his fæderingmagum wilsumne berigean ge[s]elle his feoh to healdenne, oþ þæt he X wintra sie.

Wenn ein Ehemann stirbt bei lebendem Weibe und Kinde, so ist recht, dass es, das Kind, der Mutter folge, und man ihm unter seinen Vatersmagen einen willigen Schützer gebe, [ihm] sein Vermögen zu wahren, bis dass er [der Sohn] 10 Winter [alt] sei.

If a husband dies while his wife and child are living, it is right that it, the child, should follow the mother, and that one should give him a willing protector from among his paternal kinsmen, to look after his property [for him], until he [the son] is 10 winters [old].

If a man dies leaving a wife and child, it is right, that the child should accompany the mother; and one of his father’s relatives who is willing to act, shall be given him as his guardian to take care of his property, until he is ten years old.

If a husband dies leaving wife and child, it is right that the child should accompany the mother, and he is to be given one of his paternal kinsmen as a willing protector, to look after his property until he is ten years old.

If a freeman should die with a living wife and child, it is right that it, that child, should be under the protection of the mother, and one should give for him one among his father’s kin who willingly gives surety to maintain his property, until he should be 10 years old.

note.label: compare
note.quote: In early Kent and Wessex the child reaches legal maturity at the age of 10. Compare Hloþhere and Eadric §4 [L6].

note.label: cf.
note.quote: §7.2 implies that the child comes of age at 10; cf. Æthelberht §76.2 [L78] and Hloþhere and Eadric §4 [L6]; also Wifmannes Beweddung.

Die nicht mündige (s. d. Gl 3a) Waise bleibt bei der Mutter, aber wohl nicht (gegen Pol Mai II 242) innerhalb der Muttersippe. — Die 10 Jahre als Mündigkeitstermin auch bei anderen Germanen; Amira Grundr.³ 221

The orphan who is not of age (see that word in Gl 3a) remains with the mother, but probably not (as against Pol Mai II 242) within the mother’s kindred. — The 10 years as the age of majority also among other Germanic peoples; Amira Grundr.³ 221
S. Wb: be I 2
See Wb: be I 2

‘Nachkommenschaft’ allgemein, freilich Töchter einschliessend (Toller: bearn auch Suppl.; Gegenteil: wæpnedbearn), deren Gleichstellung hieraus aber nicht folgt; gegen Opet Pol Mai II 259. Sie wird bevormundet vom ältesten Sohne, sobald dieser mündig geworden; daher ist weiterhin nur dieser als Vertreter genannt. Ein weiterer Schluss, dass der älteste Sohn aus dem Erbe die Schwestern oder gar die jüngeren Brüder ausschliesse, ist aber aus diesem Satze nicht erlaubt

‘Offspring’ in general, admittedly including daughters (Toller: bearn, also Suppl.; opposite: wæpnedbearn), though their equal standing does not follow from this; against Opet Pol Mai II 259. The offspring is under the guardianship of the eldest son as soon as he has come of age; hence only he is named further on as their representative. A further inference, however, that the eldest son excludes his sisters or even his younger brothers from the inheritance, is not permissible from this sentence
‘bleibe in Obhut, sei untergeben’; s. Wb: folgian

S. Wb: on Aa 8, wozu on friðgegyldum VI As Pro. 8, 6 hinzuzufügen
See Wb: on Aa 8, to which add on friðgegyldum VI As Pro. 8, 6

Alle Übersetzer und Wbb. verstehen zwar ‘Bürge’. Es muss jedoch hier die Bed. ‘tutor, custos’ vorliegen, gemäss dem Vorgerm. bhergh ‘Fürsorge, Acht haben’, wovon in Ags. Poesie das Kompositum leodgebyrga ‘Volksvorsteher, Fürst’ erhalten ist

All translators and dictionaries, it is true, understand ‘surety’. Here, however, the meaning must be ‘tutor, custos’, in accordance with Pre-Germanic bhergh ‘care, taking heed’, from which the compound leodgebyrga ‘leader of the people, prince’ is preserved in A.-S. poetry
geselle steht auch in Hl 8. Price verteidigt mit Unrecht gefelle als verwandt mit Dt. befehlen, Fries. fella, denen er ungenau die Bed. ‘geben’ beilegt
geselle also occurs in Hl 8. Price wrongly defends gefelle as related to German befehlen, Fris. fella, to which he inaccurately attributes the meaning ‘give’
Ags. Wbb. belegen feoh nicht auch für ‘Land’. Aber Nord. Recht spricht von ‘liegendem fé: Grundbesitz’. Dieser ist sicher mitgemeint
A.-S. dictionaries do not attest feoh also for ‘land’. But Norse law speaks of ‘lying fé: landed property’. This is certainly included in the meaning here
